title: Onramp mini-guides: capacity quick-tiles and configurator snapshot suite
creator: Ava Chen
description: Create a compact, scannable set of onboarding assets (mini-guides and configurator snapshots) to surface the minimum viable capacity choices, autoscale tradeoffs, and SLA impact during Dedicated first-run flow. Assets must fit both the product quickstart tile grid and the docs quick-reference sidebar. Goal is to reduce time-to-commit for new Dedicated customers and lower support asks about capacity sizing and SLA guarantees.
acceptance_criteria: A set of 6 mini-guide tiles (small cards) covering: baseline sizing, burst pattern, autoscale policy example, cost vs latency snapshot, SLA tiers comparison, and rollback/fallback guidance
Configurator snapshot screens (3 variants) that map customer inputs (expected RPS, p95 latency goal, tolerance for cold-starts) to recommended capacity and autoscale profile
Figma file with components and tokenized microcopy, exported PNG/JPEG at 2x for product and 1x for docs
Accessible captions and alt-text for every image asset
Design handoff includes a concise implementation spec (spacing, font size, color tokens) and a sample API payload used by the console to render the snapshot
UX copy reviewed by PM and localization flagged for externalization
decisions: Use 6 cards instead of 8 to keep quickstart grid to two rows in narrow screens
Prefer simplified charts (sparklines + single-number KPIs) over full charts to reduce cognitive load
Autoscale default profile will show 'Balanced' recommendation; 'Aggressive' and 'Conservative' variants surfaced behind 'Advanced' toggle
Color use: reserve red only for SLA breach states; use amber for caution/cost tradeoffs
Snapshot logic: initial mapping will be static table from PM-approved heuristics rather than calling estimator service (iterative rollout)

Schedule 30-min sync with ENG-40382 owner to confirm rendering cadence and caching plan

notes: Rationale: many customers pick overly conservative capacity and then contact support about cost. The mini-guides aim to nudge toward Balanced defaults while making tradeoffs explicit.
Metrics to watch post-launch: % of Dedicated signups that accept recommended capacity, reduction in capacity-related support tickets, time-to-first-query after provisioning
Risk: If snapshot heuristics are perceived as inaccurate, we may increase support tickets. Mitigation: add clear CTA 'Contact solutions engineer' and a confidence score on the snapshot
